- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent low (e.g., < 5% below 18-day min), consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean or 30-day moving average.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often underreacts — increase forecast slightly above true outcome to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates downward volatility in negative sentiment periods — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment < -0.30 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to over-smooth — use 3-point moving average of true values for correction if forecast deviates > 3% from 18-day trend.
